reflections.title: "The Lord Has Done Great Things"

reflect.text: When God brought His people back from exile, their rescue was so wonderful that it felt like a dream. For us who trust in Jesus, our deliverance from the guilt and power of sin is even greater. Yet it is easy to focus only on our troubles and hard days, forgetting the mercy God has shown us. Charles Spurgeon wrote that our griefs can never ruin our praise, but become like deep notes in our song of thanks.

Remembering God's kindness fuels our worship and keeps our hearts content. It fills our mouths with laughter and true singing. Our walk with God is not meant to be gloomy or somber, which can turn people away. When we live with real joy, we show the world how good the Lord is. That visible delight becomes a gentle, attractive witness to everyone who watches our lives.

questions: Do you tend to talk more about your daily struggles or about the great things God has done for you?
How can your joy in Jesus be a welcoming sign of God's goodness to the people in your life?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for the wonderful gift of saving us from our sin. Forgive us when we dwell on our hardships and forget Your kindness. Please fill our hearts with Your joy, so that our lives and words show others how good You are. Amen.

reflections.title: "Those Who Sow in Tears Shall Reap"

reflect.text: Serving God and caring for others often involves deep sorrow. We may pray with heavy hearts over loved ones who wander, mourn over our own mistakes, or grieve when our hard work seems to bear no fruit. Yet tears are not a reason to stop sowing the good seed of God's word. Just as farmers sometimes soak their seeds before planting, our prayers and tears prepare the ground. Genuine concern and tender pity give our words life.

When you feel ready to give up in exhaustion or discouragement, remember God's clear promise. The Lord guarantees that those who sow with weeping will reap with shouts of joy. God does not forget your labor, and no prayer or tear poured out in faith is ever wasted. Even when you cannot see the results today, keep persevering. A full and joyful harvest is coming in God's perfect time.

questions: What heavy burden or loved one are you bringing to God in prayer right now?
How does God's promise of a coming harvest give you strength to keep serving when you feel discouraged?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You that You see our sorrow and tenderly keep our tears. When our work feels hard and we see little fruit, protect us from despair. Give us patience to keep sharing Your truth with love, trusting Your promise that a joyful harvest will surely come. Amen.
